title: The Khalsa Rejects Nawabi and Claims Patishahi

blocks.text: The Singhs answer worldly offers with a sharper doctrine of sovereignty. They say the Guru had already granted them patishahi, so a subordinate nawabi is too small a thing to desire or accept.

From there the page imagines royal authority as something carried by the Panth itself. Wherever the Khalsa gathers in fidelity, a throne may be raised, because the Satguru's promise is portable and does not depend on the sanction of a court.

The rhetoric binds political confidence to revelation. The Guru's word does not fail, and so the Khalsa treats power not as borrowed favor but as a trust already lodged within its collective discipline.
